background.definition: Splenomegaly is an enlarged spleen that is usually found in the left upper quadrant. The spleen is defined as enlarged as evidenced by palpation, percussion, or radiologic investigations."Gold standard" definition is based on splenic weight, with a normal adult spleen weighing 150 grams.

list.listitem: One study found that 3% of healthy US college students had unexplained palpable spleens.
In two office-based prospective series on splenomegaly, the prevalence of splenomegaly was 2% and 5%.
Another study found that 12% of normal postpartum women at a Canadian hospital had palpable spleens.
Hepatic diseases: 35%.
Infectious diseases: 26%.
Hematologic disease: 24%.
Congestive or inflammatory disease: 7%.
Primary splenic disease: 3.5%.
Other or cause unknown: 4.5%.
Splenomegaly occurs in 7% to 53% of people with mononucleosis.
More than half of children presenting with leukemia will have an enlarged spleen.
The spleen may be enlarged as a result of systemic or portal congestion, immunologic processes, imflammatory processes, infiltration, hypertrophy of normal elements, or extramedullary hematopoiesis.

Differential.Differential_Features: Stigmata of chronic liver disease: jaundice, palmar erythema, ascites, caput medusae
Signs of anemia, thrombocytopenia, evidence of other sites of extramedullary hematopoiesis

list.listitem: Besides symptoms of underlying causes of splenomegaly, patients may complain of left upper quadrant pain or discomfort, referred pain to the left shoulder, or early satiety.

In general, percussion methods are more sensitive and palpation methods are more specific. The one-handed method of palpation may be more sensitive and specific, but the methods have not been directly compared.Percussion is more accurate in nonobese patients. See for how to perform specific maneuvers.

Dullness to percussion accompanied by palpable spleen makes splenomegaly likely, while the absence of both examination findings makes it unlikely. If clinical suspicion remains high or confirmation of splenomegaly is important, obtain imaging studies as clinical examination methods are not sensitive or specific enoughto rule in or rule out splenomegaly by themselves. If clinical suspicion remains high, obtain imaging studies.
Spleen-volume measurements by ultrasonography and CT are strongly correlated. They are accurate methods with reproducible results for calculating splenic dimensions.
Standards of normal spleen sizes have been established.

There are no studies that compare the accuracy of different imaging modalities. In general, ultrasound does not expose the patient to radiation and is a third of the cost of CT. (An academic hospital charges $570 for limited abdominal ultrasound and $1700 for CT abdomen.) Ultrasound should be the imaging test of choice unless the quality of the test is limited by the sonographer's experience or CT is preferable for other diagnostic reasons (such as staging for malignancy).
At the bedside, splenomegaly can be examined by percussion or palpation (see ).

Dullness to percussion accompanied by palpable spleen makes splenomegaly very likely (81% based on pretest probability of 11%), while the absence of both examination findings makes it unlikely (1.2%).
If clinical suspicion of splenomegaly is high based on the history or examination findings and confirmation of splenomegaly is important, order ultrasound as the preferred initial imaging test.
Once splenomegaly is confirmed by imaging, the underlying cause should be determined so that treatment can be initiated.

A useful diagnostic approach is to evaluate for whether splenomegaly is due to fluid accumulation, cell accumulation, or molecule accumulation. Fluid accumulation occurs with portal hypertension from cirrhosis or other process (e.g. non-cirrhotic pulmonary HTN from portal vein thrombosis). Cell accumulation could be due to red or white bloood cell dyscrasias Molecule accmulation occurs with amyloidosis, lysosomal storage disorders, and glycogen storage disorders.

feature.caption: Physical Examination Maneuvers to Detect Splenomegaly.

tr.td: Percuss upward along a line perpendicular to the left costal margin from the margin's midpoint
Upper limit of dullness extends more than 8 cm above the costal margin
Percuss the lowest intercostal space in the left anterior axillary line during expiration and full inspiration
Percussion note is dull or becomes dull on full inspiration
Supine position with the left arm abducted
While the patient breaths normally, percuss Traube's space laterally in one or more levels (sixth rib superiorly, midaxillary line laterally, and the left costal margin inferiorly)

Gently lift the left lowermost rib cage anteriorly and medially by the left hand. Press gently beneath the left costal margin with fingertips of right hand. Ask the patient to take a long deep breath. Lower the right hand 2 cm toward the umbilicus if the spleen is not palpable
Same as the two-handed method except that the left rib cage is not lifted
Supine with left fist under left costovertebral angle
Stand on patient's left side and face patient's feet. Curl all fingers under the left costal margin. Ask the patient to take a long deep breath
